messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — after the int8 bring-up for rwd-v2-medium we observed an AR->EN BLEU drop and some strange CJK punctuation tokenization. summary + logs below.

eval-bot: Eval run 2026-03-19T18:42Z: AR->EN (FLORES200 subset)
- fp16 baseline: 28.7
- int8 (pack-default): 24.1  <-- regression
- q4_0: 27.9
Sample artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-evals/bugs/1799999999/ (bleu.csv, diffs.tar.gz)

ken: Can you paste the exact eval command + a minimal repro for tokenization diffs?

maya: Sure — command we used:
```
./tools/eval_bleu.sh --model rwd-v2-medium --commit abc123 --quant int8 --dataset FLORES200-ar-en --split dev --output /tmp/1799
```
Sample AR source / reference / outputs:
- src: "كانت الساعة الثانية عندما وصلوا."
- ref: "It was two o'clock when they arrived."
- fp16 out: "It was two o'clock when they arrived."
- int8 out: "It was two o'clock when arrived."  <-- dropped pronoun/verb piece in several cases

Also CJK punctuation tokenization diff (tokenizer from model packaging, printed via tokenizer.tokenize):
- input: "你好，世界"
- fp16 tokens: ["你", "好", "，", "世界"]
- int8 tokens: ["你", "好，世", "界"]  <-- punctuation got merged into a subtoken causing alignment shift

- input: "שלום, עולם"
- fp16 tokens: ["ש", "לו", "ם", ",", " ", "ע", "ול", "ם"]
- int8 tokens: ["שלום, עולם"]  <-- unexpected single token for whole phrase

sanjay: Whoa. That looks like a tokenization normalization / merge kernel change rather than quant per-se. Did the packaging pipeline change the tokenizer files or runtime kernel flags?

maya: Packaging used commit abc123 (quant config q8_1u). Tokenizer files in the model tarball are unchanged compared to baseline, but we enabled a new runtime kernel `merge_punct_fix` in the int8 build to improve throughput. Suspect that kernel's postprocessing interacts with multi-byte punctuation and RTL shaping.

olga: I uploaded a minimal repro set (100 sentences) and a zipped diff: s3://redwood-evals/bugs/1799999999/cjk-rtl.zip. Filed internal issue #4527 and added failing examples.

ken: Priority? If this affects hosted customers we should stop routing int8 for affected locales. Can we rollback the kernel flag for canary?

maya: Priority P1 for locale routing. Impact is small in absolute traffic but high severity for customers relying on accurate punctuation/spacing (legal/legal-doc translation). For now we're disabling int8 routing for RTL/CJK locales in canary.

deploy-bot: Deployment event: Canary routing updated — int8 disabled for locales [ar, he, fa, zh, ja, ko] at 2026-03-19T19:10Z by ken.

sanjay: I'll run a tokenizer-level diff across full FLORES200 and produce token divergence stats (expected vs actual) and then bisect the runtime kernel commits. Will report back in ~45m. :eyes:

maya: Inline failing case that demonstrates hallucinated merge (from repro set):
```
# src (zh): "他喊道：\"快跑！\""
# ref: "He shouted, \"Run!\""
# fp16 out: "He shouted, \"Run!\""
# int8 out: "He shouted \"Run!\""   <-- missing comma after shouted changed clause boundary
```
This is causing downstream parse/NER to break in our eval pipeline.

olga: Noted also that merged punctuation leads to alignment shift and then deletions in long sentences (affects BLEU more than chrF). I added short notes to #4527 with examples and grouped by error mode (merge/punct, rtl-shape, missing-space).

ken: Next steps:
- sanjay: bisect kernel change and confirm root cause, attach simple repro harness.
- maya: produce failing test and add to model onboarding blocking tests.
- olga: prepare regression PR with repro cases + suggested guardrails for tokenizer checks in packaging pipeline.

ken: Sync in 30m in #eng-ml. If anyone finds an immediate fix (revert kernel flag) please post here. :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks — I'll coordinate with support to notify impacted customers after we have a repro confirmed.

deploy-bot: Canary note: routing change will persist until manual rollback.

sanjay: Starting bisect now, ping me if you see any other odd outputs and I'll add to the test corpus.

maya: Thanks all. I'll keep the artifacts updated in the s3 bucket and link the PR when ready. :white_check_mark:
